candidates.exact_span: Input pollutant geometric mean concentration as micro-gram per liter (ug/l or ppb) unless other unit is specified for the parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a parameter's reported concentration is interpreted in ug/l/ppb or in another specified unit changes the numeric value used for limit comparison and whether a measurement exceeds an applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) but the DL is greater than MQL, input "1/2 DL" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: When DL exceeds MQL, substituting one-half DL as the effluent concentration (Ce) yields a numeric compliance comparison value rather than treating the result as non-numeric or missing; a different reading of DL versus MQL or of the half-DL substitution rule changes both the applicable comparison value (A) and whether the case is classified as documented no-data versus a derived numeric result (C).

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) and the DL is smaller than MQL, no data is inputted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: When DL is below MQL, no effluent value is entered for calculation, so no numeric exceedance comparison is performed (A) and the monitoring period is treated as a documented no-data or non-comparable state rather than a numeric result (C); boundary interpretation of DL relative to MQL determines which branch applies.

candidates.exact_span: If a less than MQL vakue is reported, input either the reported value or "0" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The discretionary choice between the reported below-MQL value and zero changes the effluent concentration used in limit comparison (A) and whether the evidence is treated as a low numeric result versus a documented no-data/zero-input state (C).

Instream waste concentration (Cd) derived from this formula may be the basis for determining whether an effluent discharge exceeds applicable water quality criteria; different interpretation of any input term or the fixed 2.13 factor changes the computed Cd and thus whether a limit is exceeded.

candidates.exact_span: F    = Fraction of stream allowed for mixing (see "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico")
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mixing fraction F directly scales ambient contribution in the Cd formula; a different F value from the referenced procedures changes the computed instream concentration and therefore which numeric criterion is met or exceeded.

candidates.exact_span: Qa = Critical low flow of stream at discharge point expressed as the 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow for human health criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selection between 4Q3 and harmonic mean as Qa alters dilution in the Cd calculation, changing the computed instream waste concentration and the resulting compliance determination against applicable criteria.

candidates.exact_span: The following formular convert metals reported in total form to dissolved form if criteria are in dissolved form
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether total-reported metal measurements must be converted to dissolved form before comparison determines which numeric criterion (total versus dissolved) is the enforceable applicable limit.

The partition coefficient Kp governs conversion from total to dissolved metal concentration; different interpretation of Kpo, alpha, or the TSS value used changes the dissolved fraction and the numeric limit against which effluent is compared.
The dissolved fraction C/Ct determines how total metal criteria are adjusted; a different Kp or TSS interpretation changes the applicable dissolved numeric limit.
This formula derives the total-metal enforceable criterion from the dissolved criterion; interpretation of Cr or C/Ct changes the numeric limit used for compliance comparison.
